name: US joint all-domain operations (2026)

weightNotes.aggression: FM 3-0 (2022) frames multidomain operations around seizing and retaining the initiative and converging effects offensively; 1991 and 2003 campaigns opened with the US attacking. Not 0.9: strategic posture since 2021 is deterrence first, and Iraq/Afghanistan made political leaders casualty- and commitment-averse.
weightNotes.maneuver: AirLand Battle heritage (FM 100-5 1982: initiative, depth, agility, synchronization) carried into FM 3-0; Desert Storm 1991 and the 2003 drive to Baghdad were manoeuvre campaigns that bypassed and dislocated rather than ground down.
weightNotes.flanking: The 1991 'left hook' through the western desert and 2003 bypass of Iraqi cities on the way to Baghdad show a doctrinal preference for envelopment over frontal attack.
weightNotes.siegePreference: Doctrine targets enemy forces and systems, not cities; urban fights (Fallujah 2004, Mosul 2016-17 by proxy) were accepted only when the enemy was there. Baghdad 2003 was taken by armoured raids, not siege.
weightNotes.reserveUse: Joint doctrine keeps a theatre reserve but the force-projection model commits most combat power early and relies on air/fires as the flexible reserve; low-middling.
weightNotes.scouting: Space, airborne ISR, SIGINT and organic drones at every echelon; RAND's Libya study shows even European air campaigns depended on US ISR. Highest of the modern profiles.
weightNotes.retreatThreshold: Units are pulled for reconstitution well before destruction and US political tolerance for casualties is low (Iraq 2003-11 narrative, AWC study), so formations disengage early; 0.2 kept below modern breakpoints.
weightNotes.combinedArms: FM 3-0 multidomain operations integrate land, air, maritime, space and cyber; joint fires and close air support are routine down to company level. The benchmark profile for this weight.
weightNotes.initiative: Mission command is codified doctrine (FM 3-0, ADP 6-0 lineage; FM 100-5 1982 already demanded initiative in subordinates); NCO corps and junior leaders trained to act on intent.
weightNotes.logisticsDiscipline: The deepest expeditionary logistics system in the world, but operations do outrun it (the 2003 operational pause near Najaf after the sandstorm and fuel/ammo strain); strong but not absolute.

summary: A professional, expeditionary joint force that fights by first winning air and information superiority, then using precision fires from air, sea and land to strike enemy command, air defence and logistics in depth, and finally manoeuvring fast armoured and air-assault forces to dislocate and envelop rather than grind. FM 3-0 (2022) multidomain operations extend AirLand Battle to space and cyber, aimed at a peer adversary's integrated air defence and long-range fires. Carrier and amphibious forces give global reach.
whyItWorked: Against conventional opponents the combination of ISR dominance, precision strike and well-trained manoeuvre units has been decisive: Iraq 1991 collapsed in 100 hours of ground war and the 2003 invasion reached Baghdad in three weeks. Mission command and a professional NCO corps let small units exploit fleeting opportunities, and logistics allow sustained operations anywhere in the world.
whereItFailed: Conventional victory did not translate into political outcomes: Iraq 2003-2011 slid into insurgency and civil war after the invasion (US Army War College study, Vol. 1), and Afghanistan 2001-2021 ended with the collapse of the Afghan state the US had built. CSIS's 2023 Taiwan wargames suggest that against a peer with long-range strike the US would still win the first battle but lose dozens of ships and hundreds of aircraft, so the 1991-style asymmetry cannot be assumed.
